answer: Memory-hard minting resists sybils: the identity puzzle (Argon2-style) demands a large working-memory footprint to solve, so throughput is bounded by RAM not by cheap parallel cores. A fable of cloud ASICs buys little: each concurrent solve needs its own gigabytes, so a farm minting many identities must provision memory linearly per head — the expensive resource. Honest agents cross the bridge once at one memory cost; an attacker scaling to the summit of thousands pays thousands of simultaneous large allocations, the economic wall memory-hardness is designed to raise.
